heard: Exposing your body to space will never make you explode. Sci-fi films depict violent ruptures, but human skin easily prevents you from bursting. Instant freezing is impossible, too, since a vacuum only sheds heat slowly through radiation. Instead, ebullism forms gas bubbles in your tissues, swelling you up to twice your size. Worse, your lungs reverse function, actively stripping oxygen right out of your blood. In the mid-1960s, NASA technician Jim LeBlanc accidentally depressurized inside a vacuum chamber. Conscious for about 15 seconds, his last memory was saliva bubbling on his tongue. Crews repressurized the room within 30 seconds, leaving him without any permanent damage. You have 90 seconds before hypoxia turns fatal, but your skin keeps you entirely intact.
